title: Asking rents range from about $1,040 to $2,280 for a 1-bedroom, and advertised rents are usually above what the CMHC survey finds tenants pay
question: Where are rents lower, how have they changed, and how do advertised rents compare with what existing tenants pay?
dek: What a new lease costs on listing sites in 2026-Q2, how it moved in the past year and since 2019, and how it compares with CMHC's survey of rents actually charged.
leadHeadline: 1-bedroom asking rents run from $1,040 in Sherbrooke to $2,280 in Vancouver

title: With no income, a $15,000 buffer covers about 4 to 6 months for a single adult depending on the city
question: If I arrive with savings and no income yet, how many months could I cover housing and everyday costs in each place?
dek: A transparent scenario: sourced asking rent plus Market Basket Measure non-shelter costs, scaled to household size. Change the assumptions to match your situation.

leadStat.label: median months of runway, single adult, $15,000

leadHeadline: A single adult with $15,000 and no income lasts about 5.9 months in Sherbrooke but 4.0 in Vancouver

title: Pay depends more on the occupation than the city, but some regions pay a clear premium
question: What do people in common newcomer occupations earn, and how much does it differ between places?
dek: Job Bank wage estimates for ten occupations: low, median and high hourly wages of employed workers, by economic region.
leadHeadline: Median hourly pay across 10 common newcomer occupations ranges from $17.31 (retail salespersons) to $48.08 (software developers)

title: Job markets differ by several points between Canadian cities, and the year-on-year moves are mostly small
question: Which cities have tighter labour markets, and how are conditions changing?
dek: Labour Force Survey rates for 26 metro areas, with the smaller places shown on their published geography.
leadHeadline: Unemployment ranges from 4.0% in Sherbrooke to 9.3% in Kelowna (three months to 2026-09)

title: Immigrants' employment income rises with years in Canada, but the level differs sharply by admission category (economic principal applicants $70,300 vs refugees $26,400 at year 5)
question: What have immigrants admitted in earlier years actually earned, by how they were admitted and how long they have been here?
dek: Historical medians from tax records of immigrants admitted since 2008, in constant 2023 dollars. They describe past cohorts, not what a new arrival will earn.

leadStat.label: median employment income, economic principal applicants, year 5 (2018 cohort)

leadHeadline: Five years after admission, economic principal applicants report median employment income of $70,300, versus $35,800 for family-sponsored and $26,400 for refugees

title: Admissions of new permanent residents fell in 26 of 30 places in 2025, and five-year retention in the intended province ranges from 34% (Prince Edward Island) to 91% (Ontario)
question: Where do new permanent residents say they will settle, and how many are still there five years later?
dek: IRCC's 2025 admissions by intended destination, scaled to population, kept separate from StatCan's measure of who still files tax in the intended province years later.
leadHeadline: New permanent residents per 1,000 residents in 2025 ranged from 5.7 in Gatineau to 23.3 in Moncton; 26 of 30 places saw fewer admissions than in 2024
